claims.claim: Publisher exposes the six bounded classifications, records exact publication lineage, and retains reservation/CAS and inclusion checks. Ordinary fast-forward and already-included paths require no recovery RUN or additional proof.

Recovery uses current-main-bound content-addressed admission and source identities, preserves exact reviewed blobs and unrelated main content, and rejects overlap, ambiguous ancestry, unsupported modes, scope escape, changed TASK/affinity, stale bindings and overlapping competing PASS sources.

Recovery uses ordinary PRIMARY RUN/RESULT/EVIDENCE contracts with subordinate provenance metadata. It distinguishes pre-RUN diagnostics from admitted failures and returns HUMAN_KERNEL_AMENDMENT_REQUIRED before candidate creation when complete PRIMARY claims cannot be represented.

Runtime records original evidence provenance and reused-versus-executed dispositions. Reuse requires equivalent candidate/base contents, delta and proof conditions with matching raw provenance; invalid or unknown proof delegates to existing verification, and a separate integration guard remains mandatory.
Unified State selects the recovered candidate for a fresh PRIMARY review, marks prior PASS as provenance only, and ingress and Publisher require canonical PASS for the new exact SHA.

The publication workflow invokes the durable continuation for eligible divergence, resumes canonical RESULT transport without repeating proof, and routes fresh review ingress through the existing Publisher CAS path.
One publication-specific navigation leaf is linked from self-host section 7, Project Contract section 12 and README, with section-scoped retention, pointer and historical classifications.

Focused real-Git and synthetic fixtures cover the RUN-326 planning-divergence topology, material divergence, exact review binding, stale and competing sources, missing evidence, lost wake, idempotent construction and proof invalidation/reuse.

Frozen schemas and existing correction-integration semantics remain unchanged. Existing primary/remediation/repair publication contracts are retained, and TASK-326 historical artifacts and roadmap state were not modified or resolved.
